question: Should this PR be narrowed back to APK-only, or should OpenClaw intentionally support host-local certificate/PEM sends after adding private-key rejection?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not only mechanical: expanding host-local sends to certificate/PEM files changes what agent-readable host files can be attached, and the current implementation also has a concrete private-key bypass.

options.title: Narrow to APK-only
options.body: Drop CRT/CER/PEM support, rebase onto current main, and keep the tests/docs focused on APK sends through the buffer-verified document path.

options.title: Harden certificate support
options.body: Keep certificate sends only if the PR validates certificate-only PEM content and explicitly rejects private-key PEM blocks with regression coverage.

options.title: Pause or close broader scope
options.body: If the certificate boundary is not wanted in core, ask for a fresh APK-only PR and leave certificate formats for a separate maintainer-sponsored decision.

recommendation.title: Narrow to APK-only
recommendation.body: Drop CRT/CER/PEM support, rebase onto current main, and keep the tests/docs focused on APK sends through the buffer-verified document path.

likelyOwner.reason: The media-core extraction and outbound filesystem-read alignment make this the best available routing owner for the boundary decision.
